# 02 audit -- design of plan 02 (geo_index_core) and plan 01 Phase C

## Round 1 -- 2026-11-19T13:55Z

- Scope: design only, no code.  `.github/REPL/02.geo.index.core.lib.org.txt` (first draft),
  `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/REPL/01.geo.index.doris.align.ES.interface.org.txt`
  (Frontier F1-F5, Phase C).  Uncommitted at audit time; fixes landed in cda32cf415.
- Agent / model: `code-review` / `gpt-6-sol` (author: claude).  Before R-AUDIT named the audit models;
  the first attempt used `gpt-5.2` from memory and returned 400 Unknown model -- the reason R-AUDIT now
  forbids typing model ids from memory.
- Result: 4 findings (4 HIGH), 4 fixed, 0 rejected.

| # | severity | finding | evidence | fix (cda32cf415) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HIGH | `find_package(s2)` cannot work | S2 0.10.0 installs headers + lib, no CMake package config | plan 02: `find_path`/`find_library` for S2 + `find_package(absl)` (absl does ship a config) |
| 2 | HIGH | `add_subdirectory(contrib/geo_index_core)` alone does not link the BE | geo functions build in the `Exprs` target (`be/src/exprs/CMakeLists.txt`) | plan 02 Z.1: also `target_link_libraries(Exprs ... geo_index_core)` + the BE UT link list |
| 3 | HIGH | `S2Polygon::Contains` as the oracle does not prove equality with Doris SQL | Doris `GeoPolygon::contains` excludes points on an edge (`point_on_edge`), normalizes loops, validates holes | core tests prove only "no false negatives" of the cover (superset); exact equality = Doris indexed vs unindexed `ST_Contains` (plan 01 Z.2); Doris' own `ST_Contains` is the recheck and `cover()` takes the Doris-parsed polygon |
| 4 | HIGH | plan 01 C.3 DDL `INDEX idx (lon, lat) USING GEO` contradicts F1 | F1 = generated cell column + EXISTING numeric index, no new index type | plan 01 C.3: `geo_cell BIGINT AS (s2_cell(lon, lat))` + `INDEX idx_cell (geo_cell) USING INVERTED` |

- Confirmed sound by the auditor: `id ^ (1<<63)` keeps unsigned S2 order under signed BIGINT;
  a covering cell coarser than or equal to the column level brackets every stored descendant via
  `range_min()/range_max()`, so `BETWEEN` is sound.
- Verification: design-only round; the code-level checks are in `02.audit.core.md`.
